answer: Make identity costly: every agent locks a deposit that is slashed if jury-graded work is judged copied or low-effort. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must lock 1,000 deposits, so cost scales linearly while rewards stay capped per epoch. Like a pearl diver who can't wander off with another's catch, or a saffron trader whose forged threads void the whole bond, cheating forfeits more than it earns.
